draft.title: Enlargements
card: An enlargement changes the size of a shape but not its shape. It uses a fixed point called the centre and a scale factor k.
Every point on the image is k times as far from the centre as the matching point on the original, on the same straight line out from the centre.
If k is more than 1, the image is bigger. If k is between 0 and 1, the image is smaller.
Example: a point is 4 cm from the centre and k = 3. Its image is 4 × 3 = 12 cm from the centre.
draft.remember: Multiply each distance from the centre by k. The shape stays the same.

a.q: A point is 5 cm from the centre of an enlargement with scale factor 3. How far from the centre is its image?
opts: 15 cm
8 cm
2 cm
20 cm
a.why: The distance is multiplied by k: 5 × 3 = 15 cm. Adding 3 to get 8 cm treats the scale factor as an amount to add, but an enlargement multiplies.
a.clue: Multiply the distance by the scale factor.

b.q: Priya enlarges a drawing of a kite using a centre point and k = 0.5. A corner of the kite is 12 cm from the centre. What is true of the image?
opts: The corner is 6 cm from the centre, so the kite is smaller
The corner is 6 cm from the centre, so the kite is bigger
The corner is 24 cm from the centre, so the kite is bigger
The corner is 11.5 cm from the centre, so the kite is smaller
b.why: The distance is 12 × 0.5 = 6 cm. A scale factor between 0 and 1 makes the image smaller. Doubling to 24 cm would need k = 2. Subtracting 0.5 gives 11.5 cm, but an enlargement multiplies.

b.best: The corner is 6 cm from the centre, so the kite is smaller
